policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV prints the whole evening/morning saying in the text with a note that the following words to the end of v3 are omitted by some ancient authorities, so the passage is present. But both candidates carry the same wording (r01 is the same span written with an ellipsis), so the English cannot distinguish them.
ASV 16:3 begins 'And in the morning, It will be foul weather to-day' with no vocative; the address 'Ye hypocrites' that Ὑποκριταί would require is absent.
ASV reads 'but the sign of Jonah' with no apposition; τοῦ προφήτου would appear as 'the prophet'.
ASV reads 'And the disciples came to the other side'; the added αὐτοῦ would give 'his disciples', which ASV does render elsewhere in this chapter (16:21 'his disciples').
ASV reads 'And Jesus perceiving it said, O ye of little faith'; the added αὐτοῖς would give 'said unto them', which is absent.
ASV reads 'because ye have no bread' — a present of possession rendering ἔχετε; ἐλάβετε would give the aorist 'ye took/brought no bread'.
The ASV note on 'bread' in 16:11 is the gloss 'Greek loaves', a plural, matching the plural ἄρτων against the singular ἄρτου.

ASV breaks into a fresh imperative clause, 'But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees'; the infinitive προσέχειν would continue the preceding indirect discourse ('that ye should beware'), and δὲ supplies the 'But'.
The ASV note on 'bread' in 16:12 is the gloss 'Greek loaves', a plural, matching τῶν ἄρτων against the singular τοῦ ἄρτου.

ASV text reads 'Who do men say that the Son of man is?' with no 'me', and its textual_variant note puts the με reading in the margin: 'Many ancient authorities read that I the Son of man am.' The note names the alternative, so the text is the shorter reading.

ASV 'And Jesus answered and said unto him' renders the connective as 'And', which serves equally for the postpositive δὲ and for the leading Καὶ; nothing else in the English differs between the readings.
ASV 16:19 opens 'I will give unto thee the keys' with no connective; καὶ δώσω would give 'And I will give'.
κλεῖδας and κλεῖς are alternative accusative plurals of the same noun; both are simply 'the keys' in English, so the ASV wording cannot distinguish them.
ἐὰν and ἂν are interchangeable in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth' renders either identically.
ἐὰν and ἂν are interchangeable in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth' renders either identically.

ASV reads 'Then charged he the disciples'. 'Charge' is the ASV rendering of διαστέλλομαι, but ASV also renders ἐπιτιμάω as 'charged' where the object is a command to keep silence, so the single English verb does not exclude either reading.
ASV reads 'charged he the disciples' with the bare article; the added αὐτοῦ would give 'his disciples'.
ASV reads 'that he was the Christ'; the added Ἰησοῦς would give 'that he was Jesus the Christ'.

ASV text reads 'began Jesus to show' and its textual_variant note places the other reading in the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read Jesus Christ.' The named alternative is Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς, so the text is ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
The readings differ only in the order of the prepositional phrase and the infinitive; ASV 'that he must go unto Jerusalem' fixes the English order independently and renders both alike.
The readings differ only in the pronoun form and its position; ASV 'thou art a stumbling-block unto me' renders either the same way.
ἐὰν and ἂν are interchangeable with the indefinite relative; ASV 'whosoever would save his life' shows no difference between them.
ASV reads 'For what shall a man be profited' — a future passive matching ὠφεληθήσεται; the present ὠφελεῖται would give 'is a man profited'.
The ὅτι is recitative after 'Verily I say unto you', and ASV leaves it untranslated, continuing directly with 'There are some'; its presence or absence leaves the English identical.
ASV reads 'There are some of them that stand here' — a partitive 'of them that' rendering the genitive τῶν ὧδε ἑστώτων; the nominative ὧδε ἑστῶτες would give simply 'some standing here'.
